newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat higher, pressured by hedging.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat higher, pressured by hedging.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures were higher in early midsession dealings but traders said hedge-related selling was limiting the market's upside.

"We've got some good hedging in the March by Country Hedging and Benson-Quinn -- about 500,000 apiece. That's related to farmer selling, and I think it's limiting our ability to rally," a trader said.

U.S. wheat markets opened higher on export-related enthusiasm. The USDA's weekly export report showed more net export sales than expected. Wheat also was buoyed by news that India will need to import two million tonnes of wheat soon.
But the bullishness about India faded amid reports from Chicago traders that India had already bought one million tonnes of Australian wheat overnight.
At 1030 CST, MGE spring wheat was one to 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher, with Dec up one cent at $4.17-1/2. March was 2-1/4 cents higher at $3.83.
Traders said LFG also sold 500,000 March bushels. CIS and Wilson each sold around 400,000 March.
